scope.name: ai-outfitter
scope.sampling_note: No sampling: all 17 org repos surveyed (under the ~30-repo cap). GitHub `benchmarks` was renamed to `evals`; the local checkout at ~/repos/ai-outfitter/benchmarks tracks it. The local-only `pensieve` directory has no remote and is out of scope.

maturity.rationale: The org can consistently claim level 2 (delegated): 11 of 17 repos carry root agent instruction files, the org ships a pinned shared catalog (.agents settings.yml pinning default-profiles and community-profiles at v1.0.0), and the merged-PR cadence (median 29 minutes from open to merge across 154 PRs in 90 days) reflects local-agent-authored PRs with human merge. Five repos (outfitter, wiki, community-profiles, default-profiles, evals) already run level-3 automation — issue-triggered triage agents, nightly/weekly scheduled agents, and transcript capture as CI artifacts — but that is a strong pilot cluster, not the org norm: 12 of 17 repos have no CI agent workflow, only outfitter has required checks, agent review, and a merge queue, and session capture outside those workflows was not found.
next_rung_blockers: ai-outfitter/actions@v1 is incompatible with outfitter >=1.0.0; wiki workflows invoke the CLI directly as a workaround (nightly-wiki.yml comment, forge API) — v2 must ship before the triage/agent workflow pattern can roll out further
The issue-triage skill is duplicated (outfitter/.outfitter/profiles/github-actions/skills/issue-triage vs community-profiles/skills/issue-triage) instead of consumed from the pinned catalog

Only outfitter has branch rulesets (required status checks, merge queue, automatic Copilot review); every other surveyed repo returned 404 Branch not protected, and the wiki scheduled agent pushes ingest commits directly to main
Session transcripts live only as per-run CI workflow artifacts, which expire; no durable org-owned audit record found beyond reports committed to the wiki repo

repos.name: outfitter

session_capture.store: CI workflow artifacts; transcript link appended to the agent's triage comment (issue-triage.yml, forge API)

repos.notes: Flagship: issue-triage.yml runs the repo's own github-actions profile on GitHub Models, validates side effects with a SHA-pinned script, and links the transcript artifact; .deepreview defines adversarial review of release workflows; active rulesets add required status checks, a merge queue, and automatic Copilot code review (forge API). 63 files under docs/ (tree listing). Agent profile ships in-repo (.outfitter/profiles/github-actions) rather than from the shared catalog.

repos.name: wiki

session_capture.store: CI workflow artifacts (pi --export transcripts) plus generated reports committed to the repo (nightly-wiki.yml, weekly-kpis.yml, forge API)

repos.notes: Agent-maintained private repo: nightly wiki-maintainer run (ingest-or-lint, lint findings as PRs, never self-merged) and weekly KPI report; .agents/ tree defines reporter and wiki-maintainer agents and a reports skill (forge API + local checkout). Ingest commits push directly to unprotected main.

repos.name: actions
repos.notes: The GitHub Action that runs Outfitter profiles headless in CI — the enabler of the org's agent workflows, and provider of the shared validate-triage.sh script other repos pin by SHA. Carries .outfitter/skills/outfitter-actions (tree listing). Only workflow is release-please. v1 is incompatible with outfitter >=1.0.0 (wiki workflow comments, forge API).

Publishes a controller image via release-images.yml. .agents/ tree carries a researcher agent plus source-ingest and wiki skills (tree listing); 23 docs files including architecture, requirements, and runbooks (local checkout). Renamed from link-operator (owner-root AGENTS.md, local).

models.routing_and_spend_notes: CI issue-triage and the evals fixture run on GitHub Models authenticated by the workflow GITHUB_TOKEN (`models: read`) — explicitly no API keys (workflow comments, forge API). The wiki repo's scheduled agents use a dedicated OpenAI API key repo secret (OPENAI_API_KEY_AI_OUTFITTER_WIKI). Outfitter's ruleset adds automatic Copilot code review. Anthropic usage is local (CLAUDE.md files and symlinks in checkouts); no vendor dashboards were inspected, so actual spend routing is not verified.

duplication.description: issue-triage skill and workflow reimplemented per repo instead of consumed from the pinned catalog: outfitter carries its own copy under .outfitter/profiles/github-actions/skills/issue-triage while community-profiles publishes skills/issue-triage; default-profiles runs a third near-identical issue-triage.yml workflow.
duplication.evidence: Tree listings and workflow contents via forge API: outfitter/.outfitter/profiles/github-actions/skills/issue-triage/SKILL.md, community-profiles/skills/issue-triage/SKILL.md, and .github/workflows/issue-triage.yml in all three repos

duplication.description: Wiki tooling exists twice: agent-operator ships .agents/skills/wiki (with wiki-cli script and tests) while the wiki repo defines its own wiki-maintainer agent with wiki-ingest/wiki-lint/wiki-query/wiki-setup skills.
duplication.evidence: Tree listings via forge API: agent-operator/.agents/skills/wiki/ and wiki/.agents/agents/wiki-maintainer/skills/

metrics.notes: GraphQL over merged PRs per repo, bounded to the last 90 days or last 50 merged PRs, whichever is smaller: 154 merged PRs in window across the org. Median open-to-merge cycle 0.02 days (about 29 minutes), consistent with agent-authored PRs merged promptly by a human. Rework rate defined as the fraction of merged PRs with at least one review thread (38/154); 32.5% of merged PRs had at least one review. outfitter hit the 50-PR cap, so its 90-day activity may be undercounted.

recommendations.title: Consolidate the duplicated issue-triage and wiki skills into the pinned catalogs
recommendations.rationale: issue-triage exists in three repos (outfitter's in-repo profile copy, community-profiles' catalog copy, default-profiles' workflow) and wiki tooling exists in two (agent-operator vs the wiki repo's wiki-maintainer). One catalog entry consumed via the already-pinned .agents/community-profiles sources beats N private reimplementations, needs no new capability, and makes the next workflow rollout a one-line source reference.

recommendations.title: Ship ai-outfitter/actions@v2 and roll the proven issue-triage workflow to the remaining active repos
recommendations.rationale: The triage workflow is already proven end to end in three repos — trigger, agent run, side-effect validation, transcript artifact — but v1 of the action is incompatible with outfitter >=1.0.0, forcing the wiki repo to invoke the CLI directly. Fixing the action unblocks copying the one proven workflow (not new ones) to channels, deepwork, agent-operator, actions, and evals, which is exactly the automate-one-workflow-before-generalizing step the ramp calls for.

recommendations.title: Extend required checks and agent review beyond outfitter, starting with repos agents push to
recommendations.rationale: outfitter is the only repo with rulesets (required status checks, merge queue, automatic Copilot review); every other repo's main returned 404 Branch not protected, and the wiki nightly agent pushes ingest commits directly to main. Level 3 requires adversarial review as a pipeline step; replicating outfitter's ruleset shape to the repos that already run agent workflows closes the gap where it matters most.

recommendations.title: Make session capture durable before merge, not just per-run
recommendations.rationale: Transcripts exist only as CI workflow artifacts (which expire) plus links on triage comments; the wiki repo's committed reports are the only durable record. Routing transcript exports into a permanent org-owned store — the wiki repo is the natural home — turns scattered artifacts into the audit record that level 3 requires before merge and that later evals (level 5) will feed on.

evidence_limits: Local checkouts were up to two months behind origin (bash-saver, file-talk at 2026-06-05), so workflow, CI, and protection facts were taken from the forge API; instruction-file and docs reads from locals may lag the remote.

Branch-protection reads returned 404 (not protected) for every repo except outfitter; org-level rulesets and org settings (Copilot policies, Models enablement) were not inspected beyond per-repo ruleset queries.
Local-only practice is invisible to this scan: 'no session capture found' for local harness sessions means none was found in repos or workflows, not that sessions are not kept elsewhere.
Vendor dashboards (OpenAI usage, GitHub Models quotas, Copilot licensing) were not inspected; model routing and spend claims come from workflow comments and config files only.
PR metrics cap at the last 50 merged PRs per repo; outfitter hit that cap, so org totals in the 90-day window are a lower bound.
agent-operator's cluster runtime is design-stage per its README; no running cluster, deployed resident agent, or channel relay was inspected.
.agents and .github were scanned via the forge API only until the .agents clone for this report; the local-only 'pensieve' directory has no remote and was excluded.
The org has 154 merged PRs in 90 days from effectively one engineer's harness sessions; level-2 daily practice is inferred from PR cadence and org-wide harness config, not from observing sessions.
